problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{(1+x+y)^{3}},\, & 0\le y\le x, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X+Y<2).$
worked_solution:
If $f(x,y)$ is a joint probability density function for the random variables $X$ and $Y$ and $A⊂{R}^{2},$ then

$$
P((X,Y)\in A)={∬}_{A}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

Notice that $f(x,y)$ is nonnegative in the region $D={0\le y\le x},$ and the event $A={X+Y<2}$ corresponds to a subset of $D,$ shown as the shaded region below:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062830/assets/f7a0f0fb9d20a4b88d0aa4c395e2adb1d62195601ce756f57a48becc6ab38681.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X+Y<2) & ={∬}_{A}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y}^{2-y}\frac{4}{(1+x+y)^{3}}\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{y}^{2-y}\frac{4}{(1+x+y)^{3}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[-\frac{2}{(1+x+y)^{2}}]}_{x=y}^{x=2-y}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{2}{(1+2y)^{2}}-\frac{2}{9})\text{d}y \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{1+2y}-\frac{2y}{9}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}-\frac{2}{9}+1 \\  & =\frac{4}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
